title: unified rollouts: enhanced shadow/canary A/B auto-rollback and policy DSL
author: Leah Kim
description:
Motivation: production rollouts for models increasingly need consistent, policy-driven decisions across canary, A/B and shadow traffic. Current rollout logic had ad-hoc thresholds and duplicated checks between the controller and sidecars, which made maintaining consistent behavior across Dedicated/Private deployments error-prone.

This PR introduces a compact policy DSL for defining multi-metric auto-rollback rules (latency, error-rate, quality regression), standardizes how shadow and canary traffic percentages are applied, and consolidates evaluation to the rollout controller. Changes include rollout controller logic, a stable evaluation interface for downstream adapters, test harnesses for simulated traffic patterns, and docs/console UI updates.

What this PR does: consolidated policy DSL (yaml snippets) + evaluator service; metric-driven multi-metric rollback with OR/AND combinators; shadow-mode reporting (no user-impact) and shadow-fail-safe (auto-fallback to baseline when evaluation service fails); deterministic A/B weight scheduling; migration path for existing rollouts; e2e sim and unit tests; docs and console schema updates.

Checklist: - [x] rollout controller core implementation - [x] policy DSL schema + validation - [x] evaluator adapter + cached evaluation results - [x] integration tests (sim harness) - [x] rollout UI and docs - [x] migration script for legacy policies - [x] performance benchmarks for controller loop

Migration notes: existing rollout policies will be auto-migrated with a best-effort translation; any custom legacy expressions are surfaced in the console for manual review. For Dedicated/Private customers the old controller is deprecated but remains available behind a feature flag for one release cycle.

review_conversation: Marco Ruiz: Nice consolidation — can you confirm the evaluator cache TTL defaults to 30s and that we expose a tunable?
Leah Kim: TTL default is 30s; added cache_ttl config (cluster-level) and noted it in the migration doc. Updated tests to cover cacheExpiry case.
Asha Patel: I raised a minor concern around ordering of evaluation (should short-circuit when the first critical metric breaches). We should ensure predictable ordering for mixed AND/OR rules.
Leah Kim: Good catch — evaluation engine now uses an explicit operator precedence and includes deterministic short-circuiting for AND/OR combinators. Added unit tests for precedence.
Ben O'Connor: Can we add a safety guard that prevents >50% traffic shift in a single step by default?
Leah Kim: Added a rollout_safety.max_step_percent default = 25 with cluster override. Documented in policy-dsl.md and console defaults.
Priya Shah: Verified the UI editor shows translated legacy policies; migration script looks reasonable. Approving on behalf of SRE after verifying sim run results.
Marco Ruiz: Approved — all comments addressed.
release_notes: Added policy DSL for unified rollouts: supports multi-metric auto-rollback (latency, error-rate, quality), shadow-mode reporting, deterministic A/B weight scheduling, and safe rollout defaults (max step percent). Migration tool provided for legacy policies.
notes: Performance: controller loop latency increased by ~2ms per cycle under 10k rollouts (measured) due to additional evaluations; mitigated by cache and batched evaluations. Dedicated customers can tune cache_ttl and rollout_safety via cluster config.
